pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' asserts existing three items are 0 and that value 2 is rejected.
src/index.js item() prefixes '★ ' only when starred; 'AC-2' test checks exact list with one starred and others unmarked.
WHERE starred = 1 ORDER BY id; 'AC-3' stars 3 then 1 and expects id order [First, Third] with 200.
'AC-4' checks / and /?show=all both list all in id order with the star on the starred item.
VIEWS links; 'AC-5' asserts exact anchors on both views.
Object.hasOwn guard returns 400 before any query; 'AC-6' covers Starred, none, empty, __proto__ and asserts no <li>.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?show=starred'; 'AC-7' test imports routes.json and asserts it. The traffic worker passes the path through to fetch unchanged.

findings.what: AC-7 only checks the string is in routes.json; the checker script change that allows the query is covered separately in tests/traffic-config.test.sh, and no test shows the traffic worker's round actually requests the query route with its query intact (fakeApp now records it, but no assertion uses it).
findings.fix: Add an assertion in test/traffic.test.js that a round's seen paths include '/?show=starred'.

lenses.note: Change matches the spec's intent and decisions: order unchanged, query-parameter view, GET-only. Nothing added beyond the ask except the traffic checker relaxation the spec's AC-7 requires.
All 7 ACs have named tests. All four state-table rows have a test in the 'states' describe. The spec was added in the same change and the go predates the code; no later commit edits it.
Tests assert exact list output and status codes and would fail if the code were wrong. The traffic.test.js fakeApp change is disclosed and is not a loosening. I did not run the suite; CI runs it.
README line updated for ?show=starred. The 'All items' link and ★ are not described, but that is not wrong.

The show value is whitelisted with Object.hasOwn (safe against __proto__), the SQL fragments are constants, and titles are still HTML-escaped. The checker regex now allows '?' while still refusing whitespace and '#'.
No injection path: the query parameter only selects between fixed views. No planted instructions were found.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no UI framework or styling files; nothing to judge visually.
No browser flow was available. Rendering is covered by the HTML assertions in the tests.
The title and body match the diff: the migration, the 400 behaviour, the routes.json entry, and the checker and fakeApp changes are all disclosed accurately.
